- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is erratic.
- If true outcome deviates >2% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly supports divergence.
